claims.text: The damaged high-value components have coarse grains.
Previous fusion welding or service-induced microstructural degradation makes the components susceptible to hot cracking.
Laser cladding with a pre-alloyed wear- and corrosion-resistant powder will produce a refined surface microstructure.
Laser cladding will produce a graded surface microstructure.
The laser-cladded layer will have minimal residual stresses.
Laser cladding will form a robust metallurgical bond with the base material.
Rapid melting and solidification during laser cladding promotes a finer dendritic microstructure.
Rapid melting and solidification during laser cladding reduces elemental segregation.
Controlled solidification during laser cladding creates a graded transition zone.
A graded transition zone absorbs thermal stresses more effectively than the coarse, homogeneous microstructure produced by traditional fusion welding.
The refined and graded microstructure reduces the propensity for hot cracking.
Laser cladding will significantly reduce hot cracking relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated damaged surface.
Laser cladding will improve surface hardness relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated damaged surface.
Laser cladding will improve wear resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated damaged surface.
Laser cladding will improve corrosion resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated damaged surface.
The process is applicable only where the part permits laser access and the repair depth is within the effective limits of laser cladding.
The proposed benefits depend on optimization of laser-cladding parameters.
The proposed benefits may not extend to extremely complex geometries or repair depths beyond the effective penetration of laser cladding.
